approved: Explained the International Monetary Agreements Amendment Bill 2013 would let Australia lend the IMF up to the equivalent of $4.61 billion in special drawing rights, or about A$6.8 billion, for two to four years, part of a G20 commitment at the June 2012 Los Cabos summit to boost IMF resources by more than US$450 billion, and said the coalition would not oppose the bill but criticised the government for proceeding without consulting parliament.

Supported the IMF loan bill but questioned lending nearly $7 billion to the IMF while Australia itself runs a projected $19.4 billion deficit, and called for the IMF to make its proposed $4.8 billion loan to Egypt conditional on protecting the Coptic Christian minority, citing an attack on a Coptic church on 4 April in which people in police uniforms were filmed joining rioters.

Thanked members for debating the International Monetary Agreements Amendment Bill 2013, which brings into force a bilateral loan agreement with the IMF signed on 13 October 2012, allowing drawdowns of up to the equivalent of A$6.8 billion to support global financial stability.

The coalition will not oppose the International Monetary Agreements Amendment Bill 2013, which authorises a loan of up to 4.61 billion special drawing rights (approximately A$6.8 billion) to the IMF under a bilateral agreement. Senator Xenophon supported the bill but raised concerns about IMF transparency and conditions, referencing criticisms by economist Jeffrey Sachs and journalist Ross Greenwood, and asked for scrutiny of how the loan would be used.
